chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I saw Abu Sayyar Mis'ma ibn 'Abd al-Malik in Medina. He had brought wealth to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that year, but he returned it to him. I asked him, 'Why did Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) return the wealth you brought to him?' He said, 'When I brought the wealth to him, I told him: I was appointed for pearl diving and acquired four hundred thousand dirhams. I brought one-fifth of it, which is eighty thousand dirhams. I disliked withholding it from you or ignoring it, as it is your right that Allah the Exalted has made for you in our wealth.'

He (peace be upon him) said, 'What do we have from the earth and what Allah has brought forth from it, except the khums? O Abu Sayyar, the entire earth is ours. Whatever Allah has brought forth from it is ours.'

I said to him, 'I will bring you all the wealth.' He said to me, 'O Abu Sayyar, we have purified it for you and made it permissible for you from it, so keep your wealth for yourself. And whatever is in the hands of our Shias from the earth, they are permitted, and it is permissible for them until our Qa'im rises and gathers them, taking what is in the hands of others. Indeed, their earning from the earth is forbidden to them until our Qa'im rises, takes the earth from their hands, and removes them from it with ease.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on khums for wealth acquired from the earth before the appearance of the Mahdi?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the distinction between the Imam's absolute ownership of the earth's resources and the specific obligation of khums for the general Shia community prior to the Mahdi's appearance. It highlights a unique jurisprudential nuance where wealth extracted from the earth is considered *haram* (forbidden) for laypeople to retain fully until the Qa'im gathers all resources, at which point he will distribute them or allow retention, thereby resolving the state of temporary prohibition.
